name: Orientation
explanation: This criterion requires that web content doesn't restrict its display to only one screen orientation, portrait or landscape, unless a specific orientation is essential to that content. In practice: don't lock your layout so it only works one way up, and don't block the interface with a "please rotate your device" message just because the user rotated their screen. The content should reflow and remain usable in whichever orientation the device is actually in. The bar for "essential" is high and applies to a small set of genuine cases, like a piano keyboard app that needs landscape width to render playable keys. It's not a preference for how a design looks, and not a shortcut around doing responsive layout work for both orientations.
whoItAffects: This affects anyone whose device orientation is fixed for reasons outside their control. A wheelchair user with a tablet mounted at a fixed angle on their chair, or someone using a fixed mounting rig for a tremor or limited range of motion, may never be able to rotate their device even if the app demands it. People with low vision who prop a large-screen device in a stand at a specific angle to read comfortably are affected the same way. If a site or app locks to one orientation and refuses to reflow, these users are locked out of the content entirely, regardless of how good their assistive technology is otherwise.
howToTest: On a physical phone or tablet, open the page in portrait, then rotate to landscape, then rotate back. At each orientation, confirm the full interface is still visible and usable. No content should be hidden, no "please rotate your device" overlay should block interaction, and you should be able to complete the same tasks in both orientations. If you find a genuine essential-orientation case, like a check-deposit camera, confirm that the restriction is actually necessary for that specific function and not applied to the whole app.

check.question: A mobile web app locks its layout to portrait mode and displays "Please rotate your device to continue" whenever it detects landscape orientation, for no functional reason related to the app's purpose. Does this satisfy SC 1.3.4 (Level AA)?
choices: Yes, because developers can choose whichever orientation looks best for their design
No, because content must not be restricted to a single orientation unless that orientation is essential
Yes, as long as the warning message is announced correctly to screen readers
No, but only if the app is used exclusively on tablets rather than phones
